comments.content: [medium] Swapping `_APP_DOMAIN` for `_APP_CONSOLE_DOMAIN` (with a fallback) in `$mainDomain` could trigger router failures in execution paths that haven't been tested; recommendation is to revert, as the existing implementation is known to work reliably.
[medium] It may be worth either providing a more meaningful default or explicitly handling the empty-hostname case, so endpoints aren't constructed in unexpected ways.

[medium] If `_APP_CONSOLE_DOMAIN` is set, `_APP_DOMAIN` only acts as a fallback and never gets added to `$deniedDomains` on its own. Should `_APP_DOMAIN` differ from `_APP_CONSOLE_DOMAIN` (for instance, when API and Console live on separate domains), `_APP_DOMAIN` stays unprotected. Denying both domains would prevent the API domain from potentially being hijacked.

[medium] When `_APP_CONSOLE_DOMAIN` is defined but set to an empty string, the Host header assignment breaks, producing invalid HTTP requests from the empty header value. Add an explicit non-empty check before assigning, rather than relying only on `getEnv` fallbacks.
[low] Consider recording the relevant `Functions` value only when it is safe to expose in diagnostics.
